comparison: Both evaluations strongly support the monobody approach for allosteric control (C43-C58). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of citations and quantitative validation, while peer review encompasses this within their positive assessment of 'tools to control allostery' as a major component of the work.

Both support the dual-input FAK system (C77-C84). OpenEval notes the rational design using computational prediction and experimental validation, though flags C84's therapeutic claims as speculative. Peer review positively assesses these nanocomputing approaches as part of state-of-the-art tools.

Both support the extension to Src kinase (C85-C87). OpenEval emphasizes this demonstrates generalizability of the dual-input approach. Peer review includes this within their positive assessment of advanced multi-input control systems.

Both support LOV2-based optogenetic tools (C153-C166). OpenEval details the iterative improvement from LOV2 to cpLOV2 with appropriate citations. Peer review encompasses this within their positive assessment of optogenetic control tools and their limitations.

Both support pdDronpa1 optogenetic approach (C72-C76). OpenEval notes this represents a distinct strategy from LOV2-based approaches with concrete validation. Peer review includes this within comprehensive coverage of optogenetic tools.

Both support LightR development (C167-C171). OpenEval flags that the comparative claim about better spatiotemporal resolution than LOV2 (C171) lacks direct experimental support. Peer review does not raise specific concerns about this comparison.

Both support RapR-PAK1 chemogenetic system (C59-C65). OpenEval emphasizes experimental validation and biological context. Peer review encompasses this within their positive assessment of chemogenetic approaches as promising strategies.

Both support photoactivatable rapamycin (C66-C71). OpenEval notes this represents logical extension from chemogenetic to optogenetic control. Peer review includes this within their assessment of chemogenetic methods.

Both support uniRapR development (C173-C178). OpenEval highlights the rescue of FAK mutant as strong evidence for allosteric control and notes advantages over optogenetic approaches in vivo (C172). Peer review encompasses this within chemogenetic tools assessment.

Both support maltose-binding regulator (C179-C182). OpenEval characterizes this as early proof-of-concept, less sophisticated than recent approaches. Peer review includes this within chemogenetic methods coverage.

OpenEval rates comparative claim about light vs. chemical activation (C183) as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of experimental support and unclear claims about activation timescales. Peer review does not specifically address this comparison or raise concerns.

Both support foundational rationale for allosteric control (C1-C4, C16, C20-C22). OpenEval emphasizes well-established knowledge with appropriate citations and sound logical connections. Peer review explicitly affirms this as 'one of the most promising strategies' and 'important and timely view.'

Overlapping coverage of kinase biology fundamentals (C8-C12, C17-C19, C30-C32, C184-C185). OpenEval assesses these as well-established consensus views. Peer review describes work as providing 'clear and instructive picture of state-of-the-art understanding of protein kinases.'

Both support kinase structural features and dynamics (C33-C42, C196). OpenEval notes accurate description of established structural biology with appropriate citations. Peer review encompasses this within their positive assessment of foundational kinase background.

Both support computational vs. experimental methods comparison (C24-C29, C92, C187-C188). OpenEval emphasizes well-supported comparative advantages and appropriate scientific caution about validation needs. Peer review identifies 'methods to map allosteric communications' as major component with 'clear and instructive picture.'

Both support NMR/crystallography capabilities (C93-C104). OpenEval details appropriate citations and acknowledgment of limitations. Peer review encompasses this within positive assessment of methods to map allosteric communications.

Both support MSA methodology (C105-C118). OpenEval notes balanced evaluation with validation examples and acknowledged limitations. Peer review includes this within comprehensive coverage of computational methods.

Both support MD/DMD capabilities (C119-C131). OpenEval flags C125 as speculative about therapeutic potential without experimental validation, but otherwise finds claims well-supported. Peer review provides positive overall assessment without specific concerns.

Both support SBSMMA methodology (C132-C141). OpenEval finds claims accurately represent cited work with coherent description. Peer review encompasses this within positive assessment of methods to map allosteric communications.
Both support Ohm methodology (C142-C149). OpenEval notes appropriate citations and concrete validation examples. Peer review includes this within comprehensive coverage of computational approaches.

Overlapping coverage of computational method summaries (C148-C149). OpenEval finds summary statements accurately reflect capabilities and limitations. Peer review encompasses this within their assessment of methods to map allosteric communications.

Both support conceptual framework and comparative advantages (C6-C7, C150-C152, C189-C190). OpenEval characterizes these as fair synthesis though somewhat general. Peer review affirms the foundational rationale and describes work as 'important and timely.'

Both support enumeration of techniques and translational importance (C88-C91). OpenEval finds conclusion about translational research a fair inference. Peer review explicitly supports the therapeutic perspective and describes work as 'important and timely.'

Both address therapeutic potential and future directions (C192-C195). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting claims are largely speculative without clinical validation and should be identified as prospective. Peer review supports the therapeutic perspective and forward-looking conclusions without expressing concerns about speculation.

Overlapping coverage of therapeutic potential (C192). OpenEval finds this speculative without clinical validation. Peer review does not specifically address the speculative nature of therapeutic claims.

Overlapping coverage of multi-input systems potential (C193). OpenEval notes this is supported by FAK/Src examples but broader claims lack experimental support. Peer review positively assesses multi-input systems without distinguishing established results from prospective claims.
